recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. No broader Subscription batching prose change is needed for FHIR-37493; the later FHIR-50622 maxCount clarification is already present and should remain separate.
issue_request: FHIR-37493 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested clearer Subscription Framework guidance that servers can batch multiple notifications into one subscription-notification Bundle, with high-frequency updates as an example use case and a SHALL NOT delay guard tied to Subscription heartbeat timing.
initial_application: Commit c0c229792193babd9563fe660d6763e00d8a3259 added a Batching Results section to source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml with the requested clarification. The section remained in current source, and commit 7e5717da3b1419456c0ad3406f66d028fc387f1b later added the related Subscription.maxCount paragraph, but the original FHIR-37493 text copied the non-existent element path Subscription.heartbeat.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists subscription=Subscription as an active resource, so source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml is current build input. The current Subscription StructureDefinition defines Subscription.heartbeatPeriod, not Subscription.heartbeat. FHIR-I minutes for 2022-07-25 record the persuasive vote, and targeted Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting discussion. The existing FHIRcast comparison still mentions high-frequency batching, but it is no longer the only batching guidance and does not contradict the dedicated Batching Results section.
reconciliation: Edited source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml to replace the stale Subscription.heartbeat reference with Subscription.heartbeatPeriod in the FHIR-37493 Batching Results paragraph.
source_changes: source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml: corrected the Batching Results heartbeat timing element reference from Subscription.heartbeat to Subscription.heartbeatPeriod.
